documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - CARDIOLOGY INPATIENT SERVICE
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Admit: 01/22/2019   Discharge: 01/25/2019

Principal diagnosis: Acute myocardial infarction
Secondary: Coronary artery disease; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; COPD; peripheral arterial disease; abdominal aortic aneurysm (known, followed by vascular surgery); tobacco use.

Hospital course:
65-year-old man, current smoker, brought in early on 1/22 and found to have an acute MI with troponin elevation. He was taken urgently to the cardiac catheterization laboratory, where the culprit lesion was treated with percutaneous coronary intervention. Procedure details are in the separate catheterization report. No post-procedure complications; access site clean at discharge. Telemetry without significant arrhythmia. Started on metoprolol succinate. Ambulating in the hall without symptoms by hospital day 3. Smoking cessation counseling provided at bedside; patient declined nicotine replacement.

Discharge medications:
- Aspirin 81 mg daily (continue)
- Metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily (NEW)
- Atorvastatin 40 mg daily (continue)
- Lisinopril 20 mg daily (continue)
- Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily (continue)
- Olodaterol 5 mcg inhaled daily (continue)

Condition at discharge: stable.
Follow-up: primary care within 2 weeks.
Instructions: no heavy lifting for 1 week, call 911 for chest pain not relieved by rest. Stop smoking.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Discharge summary from regional medical center received by fax this AM (admit 1/22-1/25, MI, PCI). Called pt for post-discharge check.
He is home, feels 'tired but OK'. No chest pain since discharge. Groin site fine. Has the new metoprolol from the hospital pharmacy, taking it daily along with his usual meds. Still smoking, 'less'. Reviewed when to call 911.
Transitional care visit booked 2/5 with PCP. Cath report not in the fax - requested from hospital.

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Rooming: vitals done, seated 5 min before BP. Meds verified verbally. Still smoking. No falls since last visit.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM VISIT - s/p MI with PCI, admitted 1/22-1/25 at regional medical center.

Discharge summary reviewed. Cath report still not received.
Since home: no recurrent chest pain. Energy coming back. Walking inside the house and to the end of the driveway. Mild breathlessness on stairs, same as before the MI he says. No orthopnea, no leg swelling. Tolerating metoprolol, a little tired the first few days.
Med rec done with bottles in hand: ASA 81, metoprolol succinate 50 (new), atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, olodaterol daily. All being taken.
Smoking: down to about half a pack since discharge, he says. Discussed again that this is the single biggest thing for his heart. Offered patch + gum or varenicline. He wants to try on his own first.

Exam: NAD. R femoral area without hematoma or bruit. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs decreased BS, no crackles. No edema.

A/P
1. CAD s/p MI with PCI - stable post discharge. Continue ASA, metoprolol, statin, ACEi. Front desk to request the cath report from the hospital.
2. HTN - fine.
3. Tobacco - motivated after the MI, cutting down. Readdress next visit.
4. COPD - stable.
BMP and CBC today (post-cath, new beta blocker, on ACEi/thiazide).
RTC 3 mo, sooner prn.

documents.title: Result call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP, BMP and CBC normal - kidneys, potassium and blood count fine. Pt informed.

documents.title: New prescription request
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Pharmacy faxed request for ongoing metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily - hospital Rx was a 30 day supply. Pended for PCP.

PCP: sent metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg, #90, 3 refills.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed records request to regional medical center HIM for the 1/22/19 cath lab report and any echo. Second request - first one (1/28) not answered.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Roomed for f/u. Med rec complete. Pt reports no ED visits or hospital stays since last visit. Tobacco use: yes, daily.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
3 mo after MI/PCI.

Feels well. No angina. Back to doing yard work in small doses. Usual breathlessness on hills. Calves fine. Taking meds.
Cath report never came.
Smoking back up to most of a pack. He's frank about it. Not willing to set a quit date. Accepted a handout.

BP 113/81, HR 62.
Exam: Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs with prolonged expiration, faint end-expiratory wheeze. Ext no edema.

A/P
1. CAD s/p MI 1/2019 - no angina. Continue ASA, metoprolol succ 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril. Lipids today.
2. HTN - controlled.
3. Tobacco - relapsed to near baseline. Counseled. Declines pharmacotherapy.
4. COPD - stable on olodaterol.
5. AAA - due for vascular surgery surveillance; he says they will send him a letter.

RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Your recent results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Haskins - your cholesterol panel looks good on the atorvastatin. LDL is right where we want it after a heart attack. No changes. See you in August.

documents.title: No-show
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not arrive for 10:40 appt. Called, he had it written down for the wrong week. Rebooked 8/27.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from no-show.

No chest pain. Same exertional breathlessness. Coughs in the morning, clears it. No hemoptysis.
On all meds. Pharmacy fills confirmed on the 90-day cycle.
Smoking 1 ppd. Asked about a quit date - 'when it gets cold and I'm stuck inside anyway.' Will hold him to it in the fall.

BP 119/73, HR 68, SpO2 94%.
Exam: lungs diminished, no wheeze today. Heart regular, no murmur. Legs without swelling.

A/P
- CAD s/p MI: stable, no angina. Same regimen.
- HTN: controlled.
- COPD: stable, olodaterol daily.
- Tobacco: ~45 pk-yr now. Counseled, no date.
- Flu + pneumococcal in October.

RTC 4-5 mo (January, one year post MI).

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP standing order: high-dose influenza IM R deltoid; PPSV23 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. VIS for both. No prior pneumococcal vaccine per pt and old records. Tolerated, no reaction after 15 min. Pt asked about the shingles shot - told him pharmacy can give it, check Part D coverage.

documents.title: inhaler
documents.author: patient
documents.body: need a refill on the striverdi inhaler the pharmacy says no refills left. thanks Lyle

documents.title: RE: inhaler
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Mr. Haskins, PCP sent a new prescription for your olodaterol (Striverdi) inhaler with refills for the year to your pharmacy this morning. You are due for your 1-year visit in January - front desk will call to schedule.
